senses.definition: The distance measured along the longest dimension of an object.

quotes.text: Happiness makes up in height for what it lacks in length.

senses.definition: (horse racing) The length of a horse, used to indicate the distance between horses at the end of a race.
examples: five lengths ahead of the field

senses.definition: (mathematics) Distance between the two ends of a line segment.
(cricket) The distance down the pitch that the ball bounces on its way to the batsman.
Part of something that is long; a physical piece of something.

examples:
, Bride for the Billionaire Bear Shifter
His cock felt firm under her palm, and her mouth watered as she imagined wrapping her lips around his length.

senses.definition: (theater) A unit of script length, comprising 42 lines.

quotes.text: […] open your book of the play, which you have previously carefully perused, and at the same time marked with the proper calls, as thus: a length (or 42 lines) before an entrance, with a pen make a figure on the margin, […]

quotes.text: The boy was engaged to write out parts at a penny a length (42 lines) for Chetwood, who then charged the manager, […]

senses.definition: (wine) The amount of time for which the taste of wine lingers on the palate after swallowing or spitting it out, measured in caudilies.

examples: Pack night, peep day; good day, of night now borrow: / Short night, to-night, and length thyself to-morrow.

quotes.text: Was never man such favour could off atall ladies fynde, To cause them lengthe or shorte the day which they to hym assynde.
quotes.reference: 1552, Richard Huloet, “Ladies of Destinie”, in Abecedarium Anglico-Latinum:

quotes.text: [He] knows full well life doth but length his pain.
